raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #40082. A chat template can silently omit `developer` messages while `/v1/chat/completions` accepts the request. With the Qwen3-0.6B tokenizer, the resulting prompt contains the user question but loses the developer instruction.

Return a 400 response before generation when the selected Jinja template does not render a developer message. Preserve the role, contents, and ordering for templates that support it; do not implicitly promote developer instructions to system instructions.

## Modifications

- Before encoding an uncached Jinja prompt containing developer messages, render a separate probe with a distinct sentinel at each developer message's actual conversation position. Reject a missing sentinel with the offending message index.
- Use the same tools, template options, and string/content-parts representation as the request. The probe is never tokenized or sent to generation, and does not mutate request data.
- Requests without developer messages keep one render. Supported developer requests add one probe render on a cache miss; existing cache hits avoid both renders. Native custom encoders are unchanged.
- Cover silently ignored roles, content parts, multiple developer messages, original-prompt preservation, cache reuse, and the serving handler's 400 response before generation.

I checked existing work: #40077 addresses inline instruction ordering in Responses/Kimi Messages, not unsupported developer roles in this generic Chat Completions path. No direct fix for #40082 was found at submission.

## Latest validation (October 8)

Rebased onto main `71584b62c0f6c9f1a8dbad1b0a9191f775c0bcd8` at `55589f4e2db644c1de0023d5ee616a717d2794db`. Resolved the test import conflict by retaining both Jinja helpers, including the one used by the new upstream K2 reasoning tests. The production change remains the developer-message check.

The chat-serving and prompt-round-trip CPU suites pass all 170 tests. All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass. This head includes the updated CI minimum base `60878c3fba50f50978c8a38c8ea3346022bf355e`. No GPU or full-server run was performed for this revision.

## Latest validation (October 3)

Rebased onto main `10edb05e72afb79ecfdf7dbe7603f90ba05ad3ee` at `b49304c3c9f4a846246a376fae9a28a7478af842`. This includes the required CI minimum base `8854857a991e06b3ef9c4caeae34c94fc3588336`.

The chat-serving and prompt-round-trip CPU suites pass all 165 tests. All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks pass. No GPU or full-server run was performed for this rebased head.

## Latest validation (September 21)

Rebased onto main (`00986c81b`) at `03e9a1bfd2953741c00ffa3a83bfe7d3b8aa6e95`. Resolved the overlap with the new direct-token encoding path, preserving its control tokens. Added coverage for supported and dropped developer messages on that path, including cache reuse.

The chat-serving and prompt-round-trip CPU suites pass: 155 tests. All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks pass. No GPU/full-server run was performed for this revision.

Earlier validation below describes the original revision unless stated otherwise.

## Accuracy Tests

CPU validation on macOS, Python 3.12, Torch 2.13.0, Transformers 5.12.1:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python -m unittest \
  test.registered.unit.entrypoints.openai.test_serving_chat -q
# Ran 144 tests: OK
```

The suite uses its existing mocked tokenizer manager/generation and `maybe_stub_sgl_kernel` CPU helper. The added template tests use Transformers' real Jinja renderer. A baseline control with the new tests and unmodified `serving_chat.py` fails the three new rejection checks; the supported-role/cache control passes.

Separately loaded the actual `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` tokenizer at `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`: the original template omits the developer instruction; the patched serving handler returns 400 before calling generation; a system-role control retains the instruction. This checks the tokenizer and handler, not a live GPU server or model accuracy benchmark. No model weights were loaded.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No end-to-end throughput benchmark. There is one additional CPU template render for an uncached request containing developer messages; there is no additional model invocation. Requests without developer messages and existing template-cache hits retain their render counts.

## Checklist

- [x] Changed-file pre-commit hooks pass, including formatting and CI registration checks.
- [x] Added regression tests to the existing registered CPU suite.
- [ ] Documentation update (no new option; the error explains the unsupported role).
- [ ] GPU accuracy/throughput benchmarks (not run; validation boundary above).
- [x] Followed existing code style.
